identity.name: Salary Range
identity.definition: The pay band for a federal position, defined by a minimum and maximum salary, pay scale, and grade.

structure.evidence: minimumSalary, maximumSalary, salaryType, payScale, payPlan, minimumGrade, maximumGrade, stepRange — a coherent pay bundle with enough structure for a detail page.

instances.evidence: $82,764 to $107,590 per year (GS-13); $19.47 to $25.32 per hour (WG-7); SES negotiable.

purpose.evidence: Job seekers filter by salary to establish a pay floor, and use the range to evaluate financial viability before investing in an application.

sipValidation.verdict: Valid object. Federal pay complexity justifies standalone definition. Reusable across any redesign involving federal employment.

synonyms.notes: Specific to GS positions. Not applicable to WG, SES, or other pay plans.

attributes.name: minimumSalary
attributes.description: The lower bound of the pay range.

attributes.name: maximumSalary
attributes.description: The upper bound of the pay range.

attributes.name: salaryType
attributes.description: The payment frequency for the salary values.

attributes.name: payScale
attributes.description: The pay scale system governing this range.

attributes.name: payPlan
attributes.description: The specific pay plan code within the pay scale.

attributes.name: minimumGrade
attributes.description: The lowest grade level in this range. Applicable to GS and WG positions.

attributes.name: maximumGrade
attributes.description: The highest grade level in this range.

attributes.name: stepRange
attributes.description: The GS step range within the grade. Applicable to GS positions only.

actions.name: Browse listings in range
actions.description: Navigates to a filtered list of open Job Listings at this salary range.

actions.name: Share salary range page
actions.description: Copies or shares a direct URL to the salary range page.

relationships.mechanics: Automatic. Grade and pay scale on a Job Listing map to this Salary Range object.
relationships.cardinality: one-to-many (one Salary Range covers many Job Listings at the same grade and pay scale)
relationships.sorts: Default: openDate descending. Options: grade descending, series alphabetical.
relationships.dependencies: Optional for Salary Range. A range can exist with zero active listings.

relationships.mechanics: Derived. The grade range of an Occupational Series implies associated Salary Ranges.
relationships.cardinality: many-to-many (one series spans multiple grades and thus multiple ranges; one range may apply to many series)
relationships.dependencies: Optional. The relationship is informational, not structural.

views.context: A Salary Range in a browse or filter context.
views.userIntent: Find salary ranges that meet their pay floor.

views.context: A Salary Range detail page visited by a job seeker.
views.userIntent: Browse open positions at a specific pay grade.

stories.title: Job seeker filters positions by minimum salary
stories.benefit: avoids spending time on listings that do not meet their pay requirements
stories.whenClause: When a job seeker has a minimum salary requirement
stories.thenClause: They see only listings at or above their target pay grade

businessRules.title: minimumSalary must not exceed maximumSalary
businessRules.description: minimumSalary must be less than or equal to maximumSalary. Listings where this is inverted are a data error.

businessRules.title: Pay rates change annually
businessRules.description: Federal pay tables are updated each year. Salary values reflect the current pay tables as returned by the API. Historical listings may show outdated salary data.

businessRules.title: SES positions have flexible pay
businessRules.description: Senior Executive Service positions do not follow grade-step tables. minimumGrade and maximumGrade are absent for SES. The salary range is negotiable within the SES pay band.

businessRules.title: Locality pay is excluded from v1
businessRules.description: Federal locality pay adjustments are not modeled in v1. Displayed salaries are base pay. Users in high-cost areas (e.g. San Francisco, New York) will receive higher pay than shown.

states.name: Current
states.description: The salary range reflects the current OPM pay tables.
states.triggers: Pay tables are updated for the current year.

states.name: Historical
states.description: The salary range reflects a previous year's pay tables.
states.triggers: OPM publishes updated pay tables for a new year.
